Flower
flow´er
n. (the blossom of a plant; in the tabernacle, the ornament of the candlestick; rendering Hebrew perach, tsits, Greek anthos)
From Latin flos, a blossom. Scripture uses the flower for two opposite things: the beaten gold that never fades, and the flesh that fades by noon.

Biblical Definition

Flower serves two purposes in Scripture, and the contrast is the doctrine. In the tabernacle it is gold: the candlestick is beaten work, “his shaft, and his branches, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers, shall be of the same” (Exo 25:31), with almond blossoms worked into every branch (Exo 25:33) — flowers that will never wilt, in the one room lit day and night. Everywhere else the flower is the emblem of what does not last: “As for man, his days are as grass: as a flower of the field, so he flourisheth” (Psa 103:15); “All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness thereof is as the flower of the field” (Isa 40:6). Peter quotes it and adds the contrast that gives the figure its point — the flower falls away, “but the word of the Lord endureth for ever” — and James applies it specifically to the rich man, who “shall fade away in his ways” (Jas 1:11).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a flower as the blossom of a plant, the part which contains the organs of fructification — and figuratively the prime, the best part, or that which is most beautiful and least lasting.

expand to see more

FLOWER, n. In botany, that part of a plant which contains the organs of fructification, with their coverings.

2. The early part of life, or rather of manhood; the prime; youthful vigor; youth; as, the flower of age or of life.

3. The best or finest part of a thing; the most valuable part.

4. That which is most distinguished for any thing valuable.

Key Scripture

Isa 40:6 — "The voice said, Cry. And he said, What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness thereof is as the flower of the field:"

Psa 103:15 — "As for man, his days are as grass: as a flower of the field, so he flourisheth."

Jas 1:11 — "For the sun is no sooner risen with a burning heat, but it withereth the grass, and the flower thereof falleth, and the grace of the fashion of it perisheth: so also shall the rich man fade away in his ways."

Exo 25:31 — "And thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold: of beaten work shall the candlestick be made: his shaft, and his branches, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers, shall be of the same."

Modern Corruption

A culture organized around the postponement of fading — youth extended, decline denied — which makes Isaiah 40:6 unbearable and therefore unread.

expand to see more

Isaiah 40:6 is not a mood; it is a commissioned message. The voice says Cry, and the prophet asks what he shall cry, and the answer is: all flesh is grass. That is what God appointed to be proclaimed at the opening of the greatest comfort chapter in the prophets. An age that spends its resources denying exactly this — extending youth, editing images, deferring every reminder of decline — has not found a way around the verse; it has only made itself unable to hear the comfort that follows it.

The candlestick is the counterweight, and it is worth setting the two together. In the holy place stood a lampstand of beaten gold covered in almond flowers, blossoming permanently in a room with no window, lit continually. Israel's flowers of gold never faded, and they were the light the priests worked by. So Scripture does not merely tell a fading man that he fades; it shows him gold flowers in the sanctuary and tells him the word of the Lord endureth for ever. The fading is real and it is not the last word.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew perach (H6525), a blossom, bud — the candlestick's flowers; tsits (H6731), a flower, and also the golden plate on the high priest's mitre; Greek anthos (G438), a blossom.

expand to see more

Hebrew perach (H6525) — a bud, blossom; the beaten-gold flowers of the candlestick (Exo 25:31) and the blossoming of Aaron's rod.

Hebrew tsits (H6731) — a flower, and the golden plate of the mitre; the fading flower of the field (Isa 40:6).

Greek anthos (G438) — a flower; Peter and James both quote Isaiah's figure against human glory (1Pe 1:24; Jas 1:11).

Usage

"“All flesh is grass… as the flower of the field” — the commissioned message."

"“His bowls, his knops, and his flowers, shall be of the same” — gold flowers that never fade."

"“The flower thereof falleth… so also shall the rich man fade away”."
